# Expected verdicts for the gitflow fixture with pull-request lookups
# working. gitflow-expected-degraded.txt is the same repository with no
# forge reachable, and only the two conflicting rows differ between them.
#
# One row per local branch. Columns are whitespace-separated: the branch
# name, the verdict, the reason key the report must carry, and free prose
# saying why the row exists. The reason keys are documented once, in
# expected.txt.
#
# This table exists for one comparison the flat fixture cannot make. The
# default branch here is develop, and main is present and is not the
# default -- so a merged pull request based on develop is evidence that
# the work landed, and one based on main is not. The flat fixture holds
# the default at main, which means a sweep comparing a pull request's
# base against a hardcoded main scores full marks on every other table
# here: it was mutated to do exactly that and the whole suite stayed
# green. The two rows below are what fails, and they fail in opposite
# directions at once, which is what a wrong default branch does.
#
# branch                verdict  reason                   why
develop                 KEEP     protected:default        the repository's default branch
main                    KEEP     protected:long-lived     present but not the default; protected by name, not by evidence
release/1.x             KEEP     protected:long-lived     merged into develop and otherwise deletable; only the name saves it
gf-ancestor             DELETE   pass1:ancestor           already an ancestor of the default branch
gf-squashed             DELETE   proof-a:content-landed   squash-merged into develop, so merging it back adds nothing
merged-to-main-only     KEEP     kept:not-landed          merged into main only; measuring against main would clear it
amb                     KEEP     kept:not-landed          work never landed; a tag of the same name points at develop
gf-landed-on-develop    DELETE   proof-b:pr-merged        the content check conflicts, and its merged pull request was based on develop, which is this repository's default
gf-landed-on-main       KEEP     proof-b:pr-other-base    the content check conflicts, and its merged pull request was based on main, which is present here and is not the default
